summary: Colombia admits passport holders of about 100 countries — including the US, UK, EU, Canada and most of the Americas — visa-free for 90 days, extendable in-country to a maximum of 180 days per calendar year. Nationalities that do need a visa apply online for a Visitor (V) visa through the Foreign Ministry. Migración Colombia's free Check-Mig pre-registration, before entering or leaving, is optional but speeds up the immigration interview.

conditionalWaivers.text: Citizens of Cambodia, China, India, Myanmar, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam — Colombia's List C of conditional visa exemptions — need no visa for a short stay if they hold a US or Schengen visa valid for more than 180 days on the day they enter Colombia. The stay is up to 90 days. Nicaragua is also on List C, but only Nicaraguans from the Caribbean Coast autonomous regions qualify.

onwardTicket.text: Every foreign visitor must present an exit (return or onward) ticket and be able to show economic solvency, together with a visa where the nationality requires one. For visa-free visitors the ticket must fall within the 90-day permitted stay.

declarations.name: Check-Mig pre-registration
declarations.submitWindow: Between 72 hours and 1 hour before your flight
declarations.text: Migración Colombia's free Check-Mig pre-registration is optional: travellers entering or leaving Colombia may pre-load their trip details between 72 hours and 1 hour before travel, which speeds up the immigration interview; the emailed confirmation can be shown at the control. It is completely free — beware of lookalike sites that charge for it.

currencyLimits.text: You can bring up to USD 10,000 worth of any currency into Colombia; anything above that must be declared to the tax and customs authority (DIAN), according to the UK Foreign Office. No Colombian source we could read states the threshold.

source.name: UK FCDO — Colombia travel advice (entry requirements)

payments.text: The UK Foreign Office says credit and debit cards are widely accepted in hotels, shops and restaurants, and that US dollars and euros can be exchanged at banks and authorised money exchanges — not on the street.

safety.text: Pickpocketing, mugging and armed robbery are a problem in the major cities, including Bogotá, Medellín, Cali and the Caribbean coast, and criminals use drugs such as scopolamine to rob victims, as well as dating apps to lure lone travellers; express kidnappings happen in unlicensed taxis, so use licensed phone or app taxis. The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to parts of the country, including all of Norte de Santander and Arauca, much of the Pacific coast and Chocó, Guaviare, parts of Caquetá, Meta, Cauca and Putumayo, and areas near the Venezuelan and Ecuadorian borders.

tips.text: Check-Mig is FREE at migracioncolombia.gov.co and optional — it only speeds up the immigration interview. Third-party sites charging a fee for it are scams — never pay.

Do not hail taxis on the street. The UK Foreign Office reports express kidnappings, assaults and robberies in unlicensed taxis and advises using licensed telephone or internet-based taxi services, or booking through your hotel; at Bogotá's El Dorado airport only authorised taxis may pick up passengers.

Canada's travel advice says Bogotá lies about 2,600 m above sea level and that high-altitude illness is possible in parts of the country. Take it easy on arrival. The UK Foreign Office says tap water is safe to drink only in Bogotá; elsewhere drink bottled water and avoid ice.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Colombia?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders enter visa-free for up to 90 days, extendable in-country to a maximum of 180 days per calendar year. They must hold an onward ticket; the free Check-Mig pre-registration is optional.

faq.question: What is Check-Mig and is it really free?
faq.answer: Check-Mig is Migración Colombia's optional online pre-registration, submitted between 72 hours and 1 hour before an international trip into or out of Colombia to speed up the immigration interview. It is completely free at migracioncolombia.gov.co — any site charging for it is a scam.

faq.question: How can I stay in Colombia longer than 90 days?
faq.answer: Before your first 90 days expire, apply to Migración Colombia (online or at an office) for a Permiso Temporal de Permanencia extension of up to 90 more days. The hard cap for visa-free visitors is 180 days per calendar year — beyond that you need a visa.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Colombia?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from certain countries with a risk of yellow fever transmission, when you must show a vaccination certificate. The UK Foreign Office says you may also be asked to show it if you are travelling to areas of Colombia considered high risk, so carry the certificate at all times.

faq.question: Do Indian or Chinese citizens need a visa for Colombia?
faq.answer: Generally yes — a Visitor (V) visa applied for online through the Cancillería. However, Indian and Chinese holders of a US or Schengen visa valid for more than 180 days on the day they enter can come visa-free for up to 90 days (Colombia's List C of conditional exemptions). Chinese ordinary-passport holders are not on the visa-free List A.
